featured_reviews.name: Hari Prasad
featured_reviews.review_text: This review is long overdue. We've been enjoying Idli Curry Co's amazing food for the past few weeks. Ajay is a very hospitable and thoughtful restaurant owner. He always checks how far the order is being delivered to ensure he suggests the right order and shares which food will stay fresh if delivery is more or less than 10km. The Ambur biryani (chicken, mutton) and Karaikudi Chicken chukka are the best in Mumbai. So flavourful! We have tried more than 100+ options since we started living in Mumbai and hands down this is the best Tamil biryani we had. Even the wide variety of veg options (sambar rice, rasam rice, idlis, chutneys, parotta, vadas, rose milk & pineapple sheera) are very tasty. The quantity is good and pricing is nominal. We have been ordering regularly now and will continue to. Also recommended our friends to try their food and they loved it too. We hope they open more branches across mumbai soon!

featured_reviews.name: Prerna Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text: Idli Curry Co was a discovery. This is going to be a story because of the association we built with the brand and with Ajay, the owner. I have lived in Chennai for 10 years and absolutely love Tamil food- especially biryani made from seeraga samba rice. I kept pestering my fiancé for Tamil food and he found this place. The Dindigul biryani blew our minds away; it was so perfect! Perfectly cooked chicken pieces, perfect level of spice… a few weeks later we tried ordering again but Zomato wasn’t delivering to our location. Fast forward to the days before our marriage. We found their phone number and asked Ajay to cater for our all friends party. The biryanis and the starters were an absolutely hit! People kept saying how much they loved it. Now, about the food company. Such passionate, professional people! They absolutely love cooking, packaged our order beautifully and had it delivered on time. I am travelling tomorrow and I requested them for a favour to cook Dindigul biryani for me so I can carry it home 😊 (it’s their weekend special). Ajay is very kind and sweet to do this for me. Please try their food; it’s absolutely gorgeous!

featured_reviews.review_text:
In the buzzing food court of R City Mall, Ghatkopar, Malgudi is a charming South Indian restaurant that brings authentic flavors and comforting aromas straight from the southern states to your plate.

We tried three of their standout dishes:
1.Benne Masala Dosa – A true delight! The dosa was crispy on the outside, soft and buttery on the inside, served with a generous portion of ghee. the accompanying chutneys and sambar were bursting with flavor.

I had a very disappointing experience at this restaurant located in Rcity mall ghatkopar. While having our meal, we found a cockroach in the sambar. We immediately informed the staff and returned the food. Since the same sambar was served with both the dishes we ordered, we requested a refund for both items.

However, the staff initially refused and said they would only refund one dish. We had to explain repeatedly that the contaminated sambar was part of both meals. Only after other customers started noticing the situation and questioning what was happening did the staff agree to provide a full refund.

featured_reviews.name: Pavan Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
First review
The real stars? That filter coffee—strong, frothy, like a warm hug in a tumbler, cutting through the salty richness perfectly. The payasam, sweet and milky with a cardamom whisper, was pure bliss. Routine dosa didn't disappoint.

Subsequent Review:
When mango season hits Mumbai, Banana Leaf at R City Mall knows exactly how to celebrate it. Their limited-time Mango Mania menu brings together classic South Indian flavors with the king of fruits in a way that feels both comforting and exciting.We started with the ever-reliable Aam Ras with Poori — the kind of pairing that never fails to satisfy. The aam ras was thick, naturally sweet, and bursting with the flavor of ripe mangoes. Paired with soft, fluffy pooris that puffed up perfectly, it made for a simple yet delightful beginning. The Mango Lassi that accompanied it was creamy, chilled, and had just the right balance of sweetness and tang — a refreshing glass that cooled things down instantly.But the real star of the meal was the Mango Pullissery with Neer Dosa. This traditional Kerala-style curry, made with ripe mangoes simmered in a spiced coconut-yogurt gravy (with subtle notes of tamarind and jaggery), delivered a beautiful harmony of sweet, sour, and mildly spicy flavors. The mango pieces were juicy and tender, while the gravy had that signature creamy texture and depth you expect from authentic Kerala sadhya dishes. The neer dosa — thin, lacy, and soft like a delicate crepe — proved to be the perfect companion. It soaked up the pullissery beautifully without overpowering it, letting every bite shine. The combination was so satisfying and well-balanced that by the end of it, our usual post-meal filter coffee felt completely unnecessary. The flavors lingered pleasantly, leaving us content and surprisingly full without any heaviness.The Mango Mania offerings at Banana Leaf strike a nice balance between familiar favorites (like aam ras) and more adventurous regional specials (like the pullissery). The portions were generous, the ingredients tasted fresh, and the execution stayed true to South Indian roots while highlighting the season’s best produce.If you’re a mango lover and enjoy authentic Kerala and South Indian vegetarian fare, this special menu is worth a visit while it lasts. Just come prepared — one taste of that Mango Pullissery with neer dosa, and you might skip the coffee too.
Rating: 4.5/5
Must-try: Mango Pullissery with Neer Dosa

Crispy Mysore Sada Dosa 🥞🔥
At Udupi Cafe (Taste of South), the crispy Mysore sada dosa was a total delight. The dosa was thin, evenly roasted, and perfectly crisp. Masala Dosa 🥔✨

The potato masala was well-seasoned, mildly spiced, and cooked to perfection. When paired with the chutneys and sambar, the flavors blended beautifully, making it a wholesome and filling choice.
Set Dosa 🤍🍽️
The set dosa was soft, fluffy, and light, making it ideal for those who enjoy mild flavors. Served in a set, each dosa was well-fermented and spongy, soaking up the chutney perfectly. It felt fresh, comforting, and easy on the stomach — a true Udupi-style experience.
Overall Experience 🌿
Udupi Cafe (Taste of South) lives up to its name with authentic flavors, fresh preparation, and comforting South Indian food. A great spot for dosa lovers looking for quality, taste, and tradition in every plate.

Satkar Hotel, located in Vikhroli West, is a fantastic pure vegetarian restaurant, conveniently situated right across from Vikhroli Railway Station. Our dining experience was quite enjoyable. We started with a Tomato Soup, priced at ₹170, which was tasty. For starters, we tried the Veg Spring Rolls (₹270), which were delicious and definitely worth ordering. However, the Veg Hara Bhara Kebab (₹260) didn’t impress me as much—it was bland and I wouldn't recommend it.

For the main course, I ordered the Kaju Masala Bhaji, and it was absolutely delicious. I highly recommend it! We paired it with Butter Rotis, which complemented the dish perfectly. To round off the meal, we had Jeera Rice (₹190) and Dal Tadka (₹250), both of which were exceptional. The Jeera Rice was flavorful, and the Dal Tadka was perfectly spiced.

Overall, I would highly recommend Satkar Hotel to anyone, especially vegetarians, as it offers a great variety of tasty and satisfying dishes.
